findings.title: The objection begins with the moment of loss

findings.reader_payoff: The objection turns on what happens when they are lost in earth, not on an abstract question detached from their imagined decay.

findings.title: The lost image meets its owner
findings.claim: Dallalnā remains physical loss in earth, and an attributed stray-animal echo can make the speakers sound like unclaimed matter until rabbihim and liqāʾ name ownership and return to encounter.
findings.mechanism: The focus loss verb analogically touches the ownerless-stray facet; the possessive Lord and meeting are separate triggers that reverse its ownerless condition.
findings.reader_payoff: A surprising local image of abandonment is answered by a relation to the Lord the speakers will meet.
findings.containment: The animal-specific branch is an analogical echo only, never the lexical translation of dallalnā or a claim that the speakers are animals.

epistemic.reason: The trace is legacy_unbound and its animal-specific carrier is analogical; its focus word coordinates match the supplied QAC and branch records, so the bounded outlier remains visible.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The speakers' material-loss image can echo an ownerless stray that is brought back into relation.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch is animal-specific and analogical, not the surface word's lexical translation.
